message.content:
**Los Angeles (Pacific Time) vs. Berlin (Central European Time)**  

| Period | Los Angeles offset | Berlin offset | Time difference (Berlin – LA) |
|--------|--------------------|---------------|------------------------------|
| **Standard time** (winter) | UTC‑8 | UTC+1 | **+9 hours** (Berlin is 9 h ahead) |
| **Daylight‑saving time** (summer) | UTC‑7 | UTC+2 | **+9 hours** (Berlin is 9 h ahead) |
| **Transition windows** | | |  |
| *Early‑March* (LA has already switched to DST, Berlin still on standard time) | UTC‑7 | UTC+1 | **+8 hours** |
| *Late‑October* (Berlin has switched back to standard time, LA still on DST) | UTC‑7 | UTC+1 | **+8 hours** |

### Why the difference changes

- **US DST** starts on the **second Sunday in March** and ends on the **first Sunday in November**.  
- **EU DST** starts on the **last Sunday in March** and ends on the **last Sunday in October**.

During the brief overlap when one side is on DST and the other is not, the time difference shrinks to 8 hours. Outside those overlap windows, the difference is consistently 9 hours with Berlin ahead of Los Angeles.
